name: edges of a broken concrete pavement area laid on dirt: the cracked concrete pads break into the dirt in small irregular chunks with a subtle darker lip under the break, with outer and inner corners, the full interior filled with the cracked concrete slab field
label: wasteland_ruins/slab-edge

surfaces.part: cracked concrete patches and dirt ground (flat terrain tiles)

answer.evidence: This is a flat terrain autotile sheet: a full 256-wide opaque field from row 0 to 191 showing brown dirt with grey cracked concrete patches (corners, edges, a T-junction, a full slab block). The patches have only a thin darker lip under the break edges, 1-2 rows, and no vertical south face of 3+ rows. The column scan shows alternating dirt and concrete runs with no front face. It is a ground texture seen from above, not a standing object, so it reads as a top-down slab, which is expected for terrain.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts are acceptable: 5 visible tones per tile (grass reference 3, paving reference 7), 1% near-flat coverage and 0% neutral dark edges, so the edges are tinted rather than black. The picture is weaker than the numbers. The whole candidate uses only 12 colours, so each material has about 3-4 steps: a mottled grey for concrete and a few browns for dirt. The concrete chunks are pale, blobby patches with a faint light fringe. The darker lip under the break is barely visible, and no break shows a shaded concrete thickness the way the references shade their material. The cracked slab field at right is mostly one mottled grey with a few thin crack lines. It has no per-chunk highlight, no shaded edge facets and no grit variation, so it looks thinner than the reference paving, which has 7 tones and shaded stones. The dirt is a uniform scatter of similar browns, with none of the clumps or soil grain variation of the Beodeul grass. Overall it looks flatter and more sticker-like than the references, so I fail it.

surfaces.part: concrete slab patches on dirt (flat ground tile sheet)

answer.evidence: The image is a flat terrain tileset sheet, 256 px wide and 192 rows. It holds cracked concrete patches on dirt, seen straight from above. The patches have irregular edges with a thin darker lip under the break, but no vertical front face of 3 or more rows and no eave, roof or ellipse. The column scan shows alternating dirt and concrete texture runs, not a top band over a front face. It is ground terrain, so it reads as a top-down slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 5 visible tones per tile, against 7 for the paving and 3 for the grass. Near-flat coverage is 1%, and its dark edge pixels are 0% neutral. So the numbers do not show shallow density, and nothing is near-black. By eye it is still thinner than the Beodeul pieces. The whole board uses only 12 colours, so each material gets about 3-4 steps: roughly 3-4 browns for the dirt and 3-4 greys for the concrete. The concrete chunks and slab field are mostly one mid-grey with sparse light speckle. They lack the per-chunk highlight, mid, dark and deep ramp and the stone-by-stone shading of the paving reference. The brief asks for a subtle darker lip under each break, but I see little or no darker lip. The chunk edges are only ragged speckle against the dirt, with no dark material-tone edge or shadow to give them thickness. The slab field's cracks are thin dark lines on an otherwise flat grey area. The dirt has decent grain, but the concrete and its edge are the focus and read flatter and more sticker-like than the references. When in doubt, fail.

surfaces.part: cracked concrete pads on dirt (terrain tile sheet: edge, corner and full-interior autotile pieces)

answer.evidence: This is a flat terrain autotile sheet, not a standing object. The image shows grey cracked concrete pads on brown dirt, viewed straight down. The column scans show alternating dirt and concrete runs with no front-edge line or eave shadow. The only darker marks are thin lips under the broken concrete edges, and these are ground-level details. The silhouette is a full 256-wide opaque field on every row. No vertical south face is drawn, so it reads as a top-down ground surface, which is correct for terrain.

styleAnswer.evidence: The 5 visible tones per tile are in line with the grass reference (3) and a little below the paving reference (7), and only 12 colours are used across the whole sheet. The dirt has a mottled grain with about 4 tones, which is decent. The concrete is the weak part. The chunks and the slab read as pale grey with light speckle and only about 3-4 tones. Per-slab edge highlights and shaded stones are missing, and the cracks are thin one-tone lines. The 'darker lip under the break' is barely visible, so the chunks look like flat grey stickers dropped on the dirt. There is no real outline, since forms are separated by value, and the dark edge pixels carry a tint (0% neutral), which is fine. Near-flat coverage is only 1%, so there are no large flat fills. Overall the concrete has fewer shading steps and less craft than the paving reference, and the layout reads as scattered blobs more than a tidy edge set, so it is not accepted next to the reference.

surfaces.part: cracked concrete pads on dirt, drawn as a flat top-down terrain tileset (dirt field with irregular concrete patches, plus a large concrete slab block at upper right)

answer.evidence: This is a terrain autotile sheet seen straight down. The dirt and the concrete patches are flat texture fields. The concrete chunks have only a thin 1-2 row darker lip along their lower edges (for example the dark underline at the bottoms of the patches), and no vertical front face of 3 or more rows. The column scan shows only alternating dirt and concrete texture runs, with no front-edge line followed by a face. Because this is terrain and not a standing object, a flat top-down read is expected.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a sheet of scattered concrete chunks on dirt, not a cohesive 4x3 edge set. The dirt is mottled brown with speckle, and the grey concrete has only about 3 steps (light, mid, a darker lip) with little per-chunk highlight or shading. The right-hand slab is a mostly flat grey block with a few thin crack lines and no cracked-slab field texture. The break edges are soft and fuzzy rather than showing a defined darker lip under each break. Measured facts: 5 visible tones per tile against 7 for the paving reference, 1% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edges, so the outline is tinted or absent. That is not a sticker look, but the concrete ramp is shallow and the layout does not read as edge, corner and interior tiles. Density falls slightly below the paving reference.
